response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: `getCalendarCredentials` stores un-awaited calendar promises; sync consumers break

Affected:
- packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:28-30

Explanation:
`getCalendar` now returns a Promise, but `getCalendarCredentials` still calls it synchronously, so each `calendar` field is a Promise. `getConnectedCalendars` awaits it, but any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (outside this diff) that treats `calendar` as a `Calendar` will get a Promise and fail at runtime. TypeScript may not catch this if the types are inferred loosely. Callers must be checked and the type made explicit, or the calendar resolved inside this function.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// make the field type explicit and audit all callers of getCalendarCredentials
// or resolve before returning:
const calendar = await getCalendar(credential);
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: `forEach(async ...)` makes deletions fire-and-forget with unhandled rejections

Affected:
- packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125-131
- packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125-131
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553-558
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460-461

Explanation:
`getCalendar` is now async, and `await` was added inside `forEach` callbacks. `forEach` does not await the callbacks, so the surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch errors from them, which become unhandled rejections. The handler may also return, and in serverless the process may freeze, before the calendar deletions finish. The calendar deletes were synchronous fire-and-forget before, but the `getCalendar` await now delays them, which makes this worse. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all` them, or use `for...of`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }));
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Eager dynamic imports at module load defeat lazy loading and risk unhandled rejections

Affected:
- packages/app-store/index.ts:1-31

Explanation:
`import("./x")` is evaluated immediately when the object literal is created, so every app is still loaded at startup, and the load is now concurrent. This does not deliver the intended lazy loading. If any single import rejects, it becomes an unhandled rejection at module load, even if nobody awaits that entry. Use thunks (`() => import(...)`) and change the call sites to match, so apps load only when needed.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const appStore = { applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar"), ... };
// usage: await appStore[key]?.()
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Sequential awaits in the video adapter loop and the cancel loop

Affected:
- packages/core/videoClient.ts:24-33
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:480-483

Explanation:
Each credential awaits its import one at a time. This is minor once the modules are cached, but it adds latency on first load. Use `Promise.all` to resolve them concurrently.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(getCalendar));
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
